Adopt the massive free action or separate massless shell action in [[post-rpm-h-free-test-particle-action]] and [[post-rpm-h-massless-shell-action]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ an open spatial chart domain, and $(N,\beta,h)$ smooth temporal-chart data with $N>0$ and $h_{ij}$ positive definite as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]]. Take $m\ge0$ in kg and $c>0$ in m/s. On the future shell define $\kappa(t,q,p)=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}(t,q)p_ip_j}$ and the positive-root reduced Hamiltonian $H(t,q,p)=c\bigl(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i\bigr)$ from [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]; its domain is $U=I\times T^*\Omega$ for $m>0$, and the open subset with $p\ne0$ for $m=0$. Here $t$ is measured in seconds, $q$ in metres, $p$ in kg m/s, $H$ in joules, and $S$ in joule-seconds. Let $D\subseteq I\times\Omega$ be open and let $S\in C^2(D,\mathbb R)$ (all partial derivatives through order two are continuous) satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ wherever $(t,q,S_q)\in U$. If $S$ is the smooth local solution supplied by [[thm-rpm-h-local-hamilton-jacobi]] from an initial exact-graph point in $U$, and $J=[t_1,t_2]\subset I$ with $t_1<t_2$ is an interval on which its characteristic projection remains invertible, let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^1$ characteristic with $\dot q=H_p(t,q,S_q)$. Then $p(t):=S_q(t,q(t))$ satisfies $\dot p=-H_q$, so $(q,p)$ obey Hamilton's equations. The smooth ODE makes this characteristic smooth; by [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]] these reduced equations are exactly the equations of the future-shell first-order system of [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]. Under the matching adopted model postulate, this curve is a trajectory of the massive or separate massless model. The conclusion holds only on the chart and local solution interval; it does not continue through a caustic or assert a global HJ solution. It is a conditional mathematical prediction, not a reported observation.
